newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan vehicle exports edge up in August.
newsitem.headline: Japan vehicle exports edge up in August.

text.p: Japan's car and truck exports rose marginally in August and are expected to continue gaining due to the weaker yen.

The Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association said on Friday that exports rose 0.7 percent in August to 260,922 vehicles, the third straight month in which exports had gained on a year-on-year basis.
"Japan's vehicle exports are likely to continue posting gains this month and after, mainly because of the weaker yen," an association official said.
Vehicle exports to Asia rose 5.1 percent from a year earlier to 46,782 vehicles in August, the second straight month in which they had gained on a year-on-year basis.
But exports to the European Union fell 12.4 percent from a year earlier to 51,390 in August, marking the first year-on-year decline in five months.
Those to the United States fell 9.9 percent to 71,361 units, the first decline in two months.

Toyota Motor's exports in August rose 25 percent to 92,748 vehicles, mainly due to the weaker yen, but exports by Nissan Motor fell 19.8 percent to 41,095 units due to slow shipments of its Maxima model to the United States and of the Almera to Europe.
If the upturn trend continues, exports for 1996 could reach about 3.6 million vehicles, industry analysts say.
Exports in 1995 totaled 3.79 million vehicles, the lowest total since 4.35 million in 1977.
